subject: Vendr evidence reconciliation - postmortem & next steps
messages:
From: Lara Chen <lara.chen@vendr.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
Cc: michael.kramer@brightleaf.com
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Brightleaf - evidence claim mismatch (initial findings)

Hi Olga,

Thanks for flagging this. We ran a quick scan against the Brightleaf Whistic/Vendr sync and found ~24 items that are marked as 'uploaded' in the portal but for which we can't find a matching S3 object or presign audit entry in your manifest. Attached is a small CSV slice (evidence_manifest.csv) and a presign audit snippet.

Initial thoughts: either the upload TTL expired and the objects were removed by your lifecycle policy, or the upload completed to a different bucket/prefix that wasn't included in the manifest.

Can you confirm:
- which S3 bucket/prefix Brightleaf used for the Jan-Jun 2026 migration?
- whether Redwood's presign token logs were sent to Vendr (and if so, where to find them)?

If helpful we can run a deeper reconciliation on our side and share checksums/ETags to help match items. I want to avoid duplicative re-uploads if the evidence still exists.

Cheers,
Lara Chen
Vendor Onboarding Lead, Vendr
security@vendr.com

Attachment: evidence_manifest.csv
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@vendr.com>, michael.kramer@brightleaf.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Brightleaf - evidence claim mismatch (initial findings)

Lara — thanks for the quick scan and for the CSV. Copying Ben (platform security) and Jonas (portal ops) for the reconciliation and S3 log side.

Quick answers / context:
- Brightleaf uploads from Jan–Jun 2026 used our presign service with bucket redwood-evidence-prod and prefix brightleaf/uploads/2026-*/. We rotated the presign service keys April 12 but retained the same bucket.
- We have presign audit logs (presign-audit-snippet.log) and a daily S3 object listing for the period; attaching the 20261118 slice.
- Our lifecycle policy for that bucket currently has a 365-day noncurrent deletion, so objects from H1 2026 should still be present unless manually removed.

Ben / Jonas: next steps I'd like your help with —
1) Confirm whether any automated retention job removed objects in brightleaf/uploads/ between Nov 1–15.
2) Run a checksum match: we can export ETags for the suspect keys and compare to Vendr's manifest.
3) If keys are missing, determine whether the presign returned an error or the client aborted mid-upload (we should see 4xx/5xx spikes in the presign service logs).

Lara, could you run the checksums on your side as well? If we can match ETags+object sizes we can mark the portal items as satisfied and avoid re-requests. If not, we'll coordinate a targeted re-upload window.

Thanks —
Olga Petrov
Security Partnerships | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Brightleaf - evidence claim mismatch (interim diagnostics)

Hi all,

I pulled the presign service logs and ran them against the CSV slice. Short summary of findings:
- For 18 of the 24 items Vendr flagged, we have matching presign entries with a completed upload event (HTTP 200) and ETag present. The keys live under brightleaf/uploads/2026-02/ and brightleaf/uploads/2026-04/.
- For the remaining 6 items, presign entries exist but there is no corresponding S3 HEAD_OBJECT response — S3 responds 404 consistently. The presign log shows successful PUTs (from client perspective) with matching ETags.
- No lifecycle job ran during Nov 1–15 that would have removed these keys; deletion events do not appear in the bucket notification log.

Hypothesis: objects may have been overwritten / deleted by a downstream housekeeping script that runs under the Brightleaf account. Alternatively, ETag collisions or client-side multipart upload completed to a different key (trailing slash / casing).

Proposed immediate actions:
A) Vendr: can you provide the portal-side checksum/hash you recorded for each flagged item (CSV column names: manifest_key, size_bytes, hash_value)?
B) Brightleaf: run an ownership check for any housekeeping scripts (automation account) that may have prune access to the brightleaf prefix.
C) Redwood (ops): we'll extract the raw presign request/response pairs for the 6 keys and forward them to Vendr for comparison. See attached presign-audit-snippet.log.

I'll own (C). Jonas, can you take (B)? Lara, pls confirm (A).

Ben
Ben Carter
Platform Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Lara Chen <lara.chen@vendr.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai, michael.kramer@brightleaf.com
Date: Sun, 21 Nov 2026 15:45:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Vendr evidence reconciliation - postmortem & next steps

Thanks everyone — short postmortem and agreed next steps below. Putting this on Brightleaf + Vendr to execute; Redwood will provide artifacts and a 2-hour recon window next week (Dec 1).

Postmortem (summary):
- Root cause: A Brightleaf housekeeping job (run under the automation-service principal) inadvertently deleted 6 objects in brightleaf/uploads/ due to a glob mismatch during a prefix cleanup in April 2026. The presign logs indicate successful client uploads; S3 confirms those keys were later removed.
- Contributing factors: (1) no explicit transfer-of-ownership metadata recorded in the portal for presigned uploads, (2) Brightleaf's cleanup tool had insufficient test coverage for prefix edge-cases, (3) Vendr's portal manifest lacked an ingestion-time ETag field that would have made reconciliation easier.

Agreed remediation and owners:
- Brightleaf: add a tagging step for uploaded objects (x-evidence-owner=brightleaf, uploaded-via=vendr) and halt the automation-service cleanup until tags are respected (owner: Michael Kramer).
- Vendr: add ETag/hash column to upload manifest exports and surface ingestion timestamp in the portal UI (owner: Lara Chen).
- Redwood: publish a presign audit bundle (ETags + presign request IDs) for the period Apr 1–30 2026 and run the Dec 1 2-hour reconciliation window (owner: Ben Carter).
- Joint: run a targeted re-upload window (if any items cannot be reconciled) with a short TTL extension for presign tokens; target date: Dec 6–8.

Action items (short):
1) Brightleaf: confirm automation-service audit and stoplist new tags — due Nov 28.
2) Vendr: export manifest with ETags and send to olga@redwood.ai — due Nov 25.
3) Redwood: prepare presign bundle and presign request IDs — due Nov 29.
4) All parties: recon call Dec 1 10:00–12:00 PST (calendar invite forthcoming).

If anyone disagrees with the ownership split, flag now — otherwise we'll proceed with this plan.

Thanks — appreciate the coordinated work to avoid broad re-requests.

Olga Petrov
Security Partnerships | Redwood Inference
